title: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the open Zenodo archive (chronic_viruses_manuscript.zip, 40.4 MB, CC-BY-4.0, 576 files): R/Quarto analysis code plus figure source-data CSVs. source_data_FigureS3A.csv has 27,837 rows of per-visit virus read levels (RPM, reads per million) for 6 viruses, 1,148 masked participant IDs, nasal and PBMC (blood immune cell) compartments; only 4.4% of values are non-zero. source_data_FigureS10E.csv has 1,340 rows of per-participant long-COVID cluster labels. Outcome-linked files (Figure2A, FigureS6A) are aggregated per trajectory group (55 rows), not per patient. ImmPort SDY1760 page resolves (HTTP 200) but the data itself is behind access request.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the full multi-omic data (transcriptomics, metabolomics, proteomics, clinical outcomes) for 1,154 patients is in ImmPort SDY1760 and dbGaP phs002686.v2.p2 under restricted access via AccessClinicalData@NIAID with 2-4 week review. Whether participant IDs in the separate Zenodo source-data files refer to the same masked numbering was not verified.

a1_downloadable.note: Paper's data availability statement says raw and processed data are restricted access (ImmPort SDY1760 / dbGaP phs002686, application via AccessClinicalData@NIAID, 2-4 weeks). Only figure source data and code are open on Zenodo; checked the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: In the open files, per-patient clinical outcome (trajectory group 1-5, mortality) is not a column; it appears only as group-level percentages. The long-COVID cluster file would have to be joined to virus levels on masked participant IDs of unverified consistency.

a3_inputs_present.note: Open per-patient inputs are only 6 virus read-level values per visit; the multi-omic features are restricted.

a4_units_stated.note: Virus values are RPM (reads per million) per the column name and code; checked in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unit is the patient: 1,148 participants in the open virus table, with ~4.4% non-zero values; under the 1,500-row bar for regression and few positives.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 1,148 participants in source data versus 1,154 in the abstract; close enough, likely QC exclusions.

a8_label_provenance.note: Clinical trajectory and long-COVID survey clusters are measured/clinical, not model outputs (from paper).

existing_models.name: IMPACC multi-omics recovery factor (bioRxiv 2025.02.12.637926)
existing_models.score_and_split: Latent factor model predicting long COVID from admission samples in >500 IMPACC patients; split and scores not retrieved.

existing_models.name: IMPACC severity latent factor model (Cell Reports Medicine 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Multi-omic factors associated with trajectory group in 540 participants; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: none suitable for 6 virus read counts; restricted transcriptomics could use a gene-expression model but is not accessible
backbone.licence: Zenodo CC-BY-4.0; IMPACC data under NIAID data use agreement

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does herpesvirus/anellovirus reactivation predict severity across independent hospital cohorts?

controls.positive_control: SARS-CoV-2 read level versus PCR cycle threshold (source_data_FigureS2A, 1,833 rows) should correlate negatively.
controls.external_validation: Mount Sinai COVID-19 Biobank on Synapse (not checked).

honest_claim_h3: With open data only, a model could at best relate six virus read levels in nasal swabs and blood cells to a long-COVID survey cluster in ~1,100 hospitalized US patients, with very few virus-positive samples.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use levels of reawakened dormant viruses plus blood and nasal molecular profiles to predict COVID-19 severity and long COVID.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-visit virus read counts (and, if access were granted, gene expression, metabolites and proteins) from 1,148 hospitalized patients in the open table.
plain_idea.predict: Clinical trajectory group (mild to death within 28 days) or long-COVID symptom cluster, recorded clinically and by patient surveys.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians could flag patients whose latent viruses reactivate as higher risk, but the needed per-patient data is restricted.

more_or_better_data.why: Existing IMPACC models use the same restricted cohort with far more features than the open files provide.

confidence_score.why: Open data has no replicate structure to support calibrated confidence.

models_beatable.why: IMPACC latent factor models (2023, 2025) are association-focused, but their evaluation details were not retrieved.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model is runnable as a baseline and the full data is restricted.

ml_idea: Predict acute trajectory or long-COVID cluster from per-patient chronic-virus reactivation levels plus host omics; infeasible without an IMPACC data access request.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from open CSV sizes only; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Data access: the per-patient outcomes and omics are restricted (ImmPort SDY1760 / dbGaP phs002686).

verdict_reason: A1 fails: per-patient multi-omic and outcome data are controlled access (ImmPort SDY1760 / dbGaP phs002686, 2-4 week application). The open Zenodo files hold only six virus read levels per visit and group-level outcome summaries, so A2, A3 and A5 also fail on the open subset.
